pages.name: A machine and its mirror
pages.text: Lesson 1's machine, × 3 then − 1, turns 5 into 15 and then 14. Facing it, the undoing machine works from the bottom up, so + 1 turns 14 back into 15 and ÷ 3 gives back 5. Drag the 5 through to run it yourself.

pages.name: What went in?
pages.task: 8 came out of × 3 then − 1. What went in?
pages.why: Undo the last step first. + 1 turns 8 into 9, and ÷ 3 turns 9 into 3. Check it forwards, 3 × 3 = 9 and 9 − 1 = 8.

pages.name: Last on, first off
pages.text: Lesson 7's add 4, then double, turns 3 into 7 and then 14. Halving first, then taking 4, brings back 3, because the 4 went in before the doubling. Try undoing in the same order and see what comes back.

pages.name: Your turn
pages.task: Add 4, then double, and 20 came out. Build the undoing machine: which order brings back what went in?
pages.why: The doubling came last, so halve first, 20 ÷ 2 = 10. Then take 4, 10 − 4 = 6. Check it forwards, 6 + 4 = 10 and 10 doubled is 20.

pages.name: 16 mA
pages.task: The loop reads 16 mA. What percentage of full scale is that?
pages.why: Take off the 4 mA first, 16 − 4 = 12. Then 12 ÷ 0.16 = 75, so 75% of full scale. Check it forwards, 0.16 × 75 + 4 = 16 mA.

pages.name: Two starts, one 9
pages.text: The square sends 3 and −3 to the same 9. The root machine gets only the 9, so it hands back 3 both times, and −3 never comes back. A level line at 9 cuts the square's graph twice, once for each start.

pages.name: Square, then root
pages.task: −3 goes into the square, and what comes out goes into the root. What comes back?
pages.why: −3 squared is 9. The root gets only that 9 and hands back its positive root, 3. Nothing in the 9 says a minus went in.

pages.name: The lock
pages.text: Lock the square's input to 0 and up, and each output comes from one input again, so the root gives back every start. A flow meter is locked already: flow, as a fraction of full, runs from 0 to 1 and never goes below 0. So a flow of 0.707 squares to 0.5 pressure difference, and the root gives back 0.707, 71% flow.

pages.name: The heater
pages.task: An example 16 Ω heater makes 3600 W. Its machine squares the current, then multiplies by 16. What current is flowing?
pages.why: The × 16 came last, so undo it first, 3600 ÷ 16 = 225. Then the root, √225 = 15 A. The lock keeps the current 0 and up, so the root undoes the square.

pages.name: Square or cube?
pages.task: Which machine can be undone with no lock?
pages.why: The cube sends 2 to 8 and −2 to −8, two different outputs, so each output comes from one input. Each of its level lines cuts once, as in lesson 3. The square sends 2 and −2 to the same 4.
pages.alt: Two graphs. The square, with inputs from −2.5 to 2.5, and the cube. A level line at 4 cuts the square twice, at −2 and 2. Level lines at 8 and −8 each cut the cube once.

pages.name: The mirror
pages.text: On one grid, `f(x) = 3x − 1` takes 5 to 14, so `f⁻¹` takes 14 back to 5, and a graph plots input across and output up, so (5, 14) on `f` becomes (14, 5) on `f⁻¹`. Every point swaps its two numbers like this, so the two graphs are mirror images in the dashed line `y = x`, as the exponential and the logarithm will be in Exponentials and logarithms. Drag the point along `f` to see another pair swap.
